The April30,2026 House question was passage of H.R.7567 as amended,224-200 with6 Not Voting. This is one whole farm/food/rural-development package, including commodity, conservation, credit, trade, forestry, energy, agricultural research, regulation and crop-insurance provisions as well as the Health and social-support mechanisms below. It is not a standalone SNAP or rural-health vote. H.Res.1224 and the April29 Record establish the deemed base as Print119-22 modified by report119-628 PartA; the April30 Record establishes amendment disposition and final passage. The governed EH supplies the operative package text. Its separate adopted hot-chicken and demonstration-report amendments remain individually recorded choices145/146; failed soda amendment151 is not a passed component. Voice/unrecorded amendment outcomes do not create individual member positions. H.Res.1224 section11 orders the Clerk to await H.R.1346 and conditionally append that bill as passed. That prospective engrossment instruction does not establish passage or inclusion of H.R.1346 at this recorded question; no future text is borrowed into this meaning. Subsequent technical engrossment corrections are authorized in the April30 Record, not a separate policy vote.

TitleIV extends or revises household nutrition-assistance programs and administration. Section4102 removes the fiscal2023 sunset on the EBT switching/routing-fee prohibition; the separate interchange-fee bar remains.4103 permits reasonable-cost State contracting for certification/other functions under specified backlog, error-rate or application-increase conditions. It requires merit-principle adherence, no incentives to deny/delay eligible benefits, no contractor financial interest in a retailer, a blended workforce without displacement of merit staff, notification/public information within10days and annual reporting. Its temporary backlog/error-rate expiry conditions and collective-bargaining savings remain. Contracting is permission, not a mandated benefit denial, eligibility reduction or replacement of every State employee.4104 limits the six-month new retailer-application bar to denials on two consecutive occasions within three years; it does not repeal trafficking sanctions generally.4105 adds below-tolerance errors to supplemental reporting without changing the payment-error tolerance calculation.4106/4107 extend printed SNAP/anti-trafficking authority dates to2031.4108 requires proposed EBT security regulations within six months;4109 requires an administrative-cost study within12months. Neither demonstrates deployed protections or reduced costs.

4110 adds animal protein to the incentive-food category within the existing retailer waiver process, retaining the underlying staple-food/current-dietary-recommendation condition and the prohibition on limiting SNAP benefit use. This is an incentive mechanism, not an animal-protein-only benefit or a general food-definition rewrite.4111 moves online purchasing toward a permanent program, with a transition starting within120days and regulations within two years, consumer protections and rural equitable-access considerations.4112 extends food-assistance infrastructure/commodity authorities and permits a State to request up to20percent of its allocated commodity costs through DoD Fresh.4113 extends the Indian-reservation food-procurement demonstration.4114 adds hot rotisserie chicken to2012(k)'s hot-food exceptions, preserving the other conditional meal pathways.4115 requires a feasibility/implementation/effectiveness and recommendation report within120days after ALL food-definition demonstrations conclude; it neither creates demonstration authority nor enacts a food restriction. The failed PartB amendment47 soda exclusion is absent.

4201 retains the senior farmers-market program's mandatory$20.6million annually for2027-2031 and adds maple syrup/tree nuts to the named foods; existing low-income-senior, fresh/local/unprepared-food and benefit-resource/tax protections remain.4202 extends CSFP and creates a delivery pilot with$10million authorized annually for2027-2031, available until spent, with per-State awards capped at the lesser of$4million or the greater of caseload-times$60 and$10,000. Competitive local distribution prioritizes rural areas and permits delivery, staff, transportation and outreach uses. This is not an individual$10million benefit.4204's Tribal CSFP pilot requires$1million appropriated specifically in advance, selection/capacity and procurement conditions, domestic commodities, no material food-package increase and nutrition/Tribal-significance criteria; separate staffing authority is$1.2million annually for2027-2031.4203/4301 extend special nutrition-project and school fresh-produce authorities.

4302 requires at least95percent domestic purchases in EACH designated AMS food category for school food authorities within the retained1760(n) scope, beginning the first school year after enactment. Listed domestically unavailable products are excluded from the calculation; waiver/accommodation authority is restricted. It bars raw/processed poultry and seafood imports from China/Russia. The underlying contiguous-US purchase limitation and separate Hawaii/Puerto Rico rules remain; this is not an unqualified nationwide95percent of all spending rule.4303 preserves GusNIP nutrition incentives and produce-prescription programs, adds all-forms fruit/vegetable priority to incentive grants and broadens produce prescriptions to all forms of fruits, vegetables and legumes. It retains the50percent Federal grant share with existing Tribal matching provisions and adds a discretionary poverty-area waiver. The prescription program still requires a health-care partner and evaluation/coordination conditions. A participant must both be eligible for SNAP benefits or eligible for and enrolled in Medicaid, and belong to a low-income household that has, or is at risk of developing, a diet-related health condition. Printed authorization/administrative dates extend to2031; existing mandatory program amounts are not all replaced or newly appropriated.4305 broadens dairy incentives to qualifying cheese/yogurt and all specified pasteurized vitaminA/D fluid milk varieties, with yogurt added-sugar limits, and raises authorization to$50million available until expended only if appropriated in advance. That is one authorization, not$50million annually or a limit on ordinary SNAP purchases.

4306 authorizes$200million annually for2027-2031 for State/local-farmer food cooperative agreements to procure unprocessed/minimally processed local food and distribute it through proven food-access organizations. Local means within400miles or the defined entity boundaries; at least25percent of annual product value must come from designated small/midsize/beginning/veteran producers. Administrative/technical-assistance caps,10percent Tribal allocation,1percent of the remainder per non-Tribal State and the existing60percent-poverty/40percent-unemployment remainder formula delimit the program.4307 raises Healthy Food Financing's single authorization from$125million to$135million, available until spent, for eligible underserved-area food-retail/enterprise financing rather than direct household cash.4308 replaces the five-year dietary-guideline cycle with a2030 report and at least ten-year intervals, permitting earlier necessary scientific/health updates. The2025 report controls until the first compliant replacement. Independent-board, disclosure, scientific-review and topic-exclusion requirements remain; guidance is not a self-executing SNAP food ban.4309 directs low-risk categorization/regulatory coordination for fresh/raw/minimally processed produce in childcare, with provider compliance/penalty protections and discretionary State-fund withholding.4310 creates practicable common application OR information-sharing and payment-equipment provisions across named SNAP/WIC/farmers-market/Gus programs. Its unrecorded amendment origin does not establish an individual vote on those enrollment provisions.

Rural-care provisions are separate components of the same package.6101 broadens existing temporary telemedicine and community-facility priorities to rural health facilities and mental, behavioral and maternal-health needs, retaining the existing20percent telemedicine set-aside and insufficient-qualified-applicant exception; the printed priority period extends through2027.6102 authorizes$82million annually for2027-2031 for distance learning and telemedicine, with appropriated funds available for the following two fiscal years, not medical-only spending or guaranteed treatment.5107 permits Farm Credit institutions to finance eligible essential community facilities, with a15percent outstanding-loan ceiling and opportunity for other lenders; it is not guaranteed lending.6305 prioritizes qualified rural childcare projects through four existing programs for2027-2029, with licensing/health-safety requirements, geographic balancing and evaluation/reporting, without creating a universal childcare entitlement.6308 requires rural-health-liaison coordination/reporting on farm stress services.

6417 expands existing rural-hospital refinancing to the ten defined health-facility types, including rural clinics, critical-access/rural-emergency facilities, home-health agencies and community health centers. Resources, financial-hardship/stability, planning and existing preservation-of-care-access/financial-feasibility/security conditions delimit assistance. The Secretary MAY waive the named inability-to-obtain-other-credit condition for an insolvent facility, not all loan conditions. Program-specific rural/population exceptions remain; eligibility is not uniformly every facility in any place below50,000 people. Tailored technical assistance may address construction, telehealth, records, finance and grant/loan access, with priority for existing borrowers/grantees and no more than$2million annually authorized for2027-2031. These changes take effect upon completion of rulemaking.6423 extends the existing regional Delta consortium health-care/public-health-services/education authority at$3million annually for2027-2031; it is not nationwide universal coverage.

7108 extends the separate expanded food/nutrition education program's$90million annual authorization through2031 for direct low-income-family nutrition education. It does not restore SNAP-Ed's2036a grants eliminated after fiscal2025 by Public Law119-21.7204 extends existing pulse-crop health/nutrition research ($25million annually) and the Comprehensive Food Safety Training Network ($20million annually, until spent) through2031 alongside agricultural research changes; animal/crop health and exposure research are not patient-care guarantees.7209 adds education/support for youth and young adults with disabilities interested in farming and extends AgrAbility's$5million annual authority, retaining rehabilitation/referral, farmer-family and veteran safeguards.7402 extends the Farm and Ranch Stress Assistance Network's$10million annual authority, adds crisis hotlines, permits referral partnerships with specified clinical providers and requires a two-year farmer/rancher mental/tele-mental-health availability/use assessment. Service coordination and reports do not assure each person treatment.12407 extends the$3million annual emergency/transitional pet-shelter/housing grant authority through2031 for defined domestic/dating-violence, sexual-assault and stalking victims with animals. Existing24month assistance plus conditional six-month extension, confidentiality, no mandatory services/protective-order/criminal-justice-participation conditions and administrative cap remain.12410 extends already-enacted Public Law119-69 school-lunch milk/nondairy options, substitution protections, sales rules and milk-fat saturated-fat treatment to school breakfast. It permits whole milk; it does not require every child to drink it or newly create lunch authority.

TitleIII changes international food assistance as part of the wider package.3101 transfers the defined Food for Peace authorities/assets/liabilities from USAID to USDA at enactment, covering authorities held fromJanuary1,2026 onward, with State consultation.3102 narrows emergency overriding authority from any other LAW to this ACT, adds eligible NGOs and limits non-US-commodity/ocean-transport expenses to50percent of available TitleII funds.3103 repeals1724's tonnage/nonemergency and processed/fortified/bagged-commodity minima with their waivers; it does not repeal every dollar minimum.3110 retains the nonemergency$365million floor/30percent ceiling and adds$200million annually for2027-2031 from emergency TitleII funds for ready-to-use therapeutic child-wasting food ONLY when the latest specified under-five wasting estimate exceeds5percent AND annual TitleII funds exceed$1.2billion. This uses available funds, not a new unconditional appropriation.3106 requires at least$15million annually for2027-2031 from available TitleII funds for the food-relief partnership, available until spent; related consultation, quality and oversight/reporting remain.3308 extends McGovern-Dole and changes developing-country local/regional procurement from up-to10percent to8-15percent. Adding lower-middle-income countries concerns payment of internal transport/storage/handling costs under1736o-1(c)(2)(B), not general eligibility for every food-assistance activity; underlying poverty/net-food-import/education conditions remain. These programs include school food and defined child/pregnant/nursing nutrition assistance, not evidence that assistance was delivered.

The temporal baseline matters. Public Law119-37 section5002 already extends specified2018 farm authorities through the later ofSeptember30,2026 or later applicable statutory dates, subject to its exceptions and appropriation conditions. Printed2023 expiries in amended clauses do not establish that every program had already ended. Public Law119-21's prior SNAP eligibility/work-rule/cost-sharing and SNAP-Ed changes are distinct current law; this passage vote does not newly enact those earlier changes or repeal them wholesale. Floor opponents opposed the package and argued that it fails to undo earlier SNAP cuts and permits problematic contracting; floor proponents defended the provisions and urged passage. These are attributed competing arguments, not adopted fiscal/participation estimates, causal findings, motives or proof of health outcomes. Adopted Luna28 removed the three specified pesticide regulatory/liability sections before passage; the earlier general debate about those sections cannot establish that they remained in the final package. The floor opponent's inserted relief/recommittal text was an unoffered alternative; roll153 is a failed bare recommittal, not support/opposition to that printed substitute.

A Yea supported passage of this entire exact farm package, including its qualified nutrition, rural-care and social-service provisions. A Nay opposed passage of that package. Neither establishes separate positions on SNAP contracting, hot chicken, food guidelines, clinical refinancing, pesticides or any other component, or a preferred alternative. House passage is not enactment, funded awards, restored benefits, achieved food/care access or predicted fiscal/nutrition outcomes.

Immigration qualification of this same whole-passage choice is grounded in the explicit loan eligibility operators, with the other cross-border and personal-status references kept in their own scopes. The complete 959629-character governed EH was read through the attestation and footer. That reading is not an independent raw-HTML or complete Congressional Record reconstruction, a certificate of current-law integration, or editorial acceptance. All original unapproved Health meaning, source identities, claim bindings and limitations above remain part of this same core. Yea supports and Nay opposes passage of the entire package; neither establishes a separate position on any mechanism below.

Sections5101 and5201 replace each printed 'a majority' in the second sentence of7USC1922(a)(1) and1941(a)(1) with 'at least a 50 percent'. In the separately retained2024 statutory parents, that sentence applies conditions including United States citizenship to individual applicants and, for the named entity forms, individuals holding the specified interest. The proposal changes that statutory interest threshold, including the exactly50percent boundary, without deleting the citizenship words or converting every other condition into citizenship. Direct-loan experience, family-farm/operator and inability-to-obtain-credit predicates remain distinct. Section5301 likewise replaces the printed majority threshold in the first sentence of1961(a), whose individual and entity-interest clauses include citizenship, while reorganizing that subsection. This is a source-grounded reason to propose Immigration membership; it is not a conclusion that a particular noncitizen becomes eligible, that only citizens currently qualify, or that the bill supplies immigration status or work authorization.

The loan baselines have a material qualification: the separately preserved January1,2024 direct-loan regulation764.101(c) also names United States noncitizen nationals and qualified aliens for applicants and note signers. The guaranteed-loan regulation762.120(d) separately names those classes, requires the majority entity interest to be held by members in the listed classes, and requires appropriate immigration-status documentation for noncitizen nationals and qualified aliens. These are dated regulatory comparators, not a substituted text of the bill's statutory amendments or an adjudication of their interaction. Later regulations, other controlling law, exact entity structures, signature obligations and individual applications remain for legal/source review. No numerical beneficial-ownership calculation or beneficiary finding is made.

The adjacent loan operators must not be collapsed into that threshold.5101 adds qualified-operator, operating-only entity and embedded-entity rules. Its operating-only rule requires one or more real-estate owners to own at least50percent, or the other percentage the Secretary determines appropriate, of the applicant; its embedded rule retains the at-least75percent condition in its own terms.5201 changes its own operating-loan paragraph and5301 supplies separate emergency-loan rules. In the dated1961(a) parent, the fifth sentence deleted by5301 is the embedded-entity direct-ownership sentence; the bill adds replacement special rules rather than deleting citizenship or all disaster/credit predicates.12420 separately brings defined commercial fishing and fish processing into the named loan definitions and purposes, with different permitted ownership-loan and operating-loan uses and implementation steps. These provisions do not establish that every fishery participant receives a loan or that personal eligibility predicates are waived.

3306 creates a two-way agricultural cultural-immersion and exchange program. The outgoing eligible candidate must meet all four printed conditions: age19-30, demonstrated relevant experience, preparation to live in one or more host countries for the printed two-to-six-month period, and United States residence. Incoming placement in United States host families expressly requires the age condition and residence in an eligible country; it does not simply import all four outgoing conditions. The purpose's reference to developing United States citizens does not rewrite the eligibility word 'resident' into 'citizen'. Eligible countries have agricultural trade relations recognized by the named Service. Administration requires a qualified nonprofit cooperative agreement, the specified memorandum-of-understanding priority and equal non-Federal matching funds.10million dollars annually for2027-2031 is authorization, not proof of appropriation, placement, visa issuance, admission or work permission.7118's separate international institutional partnerships and outgoing internships/fellowships likewise do not themselves establish personal admission status.

2502(g) and8507 provide different discretionary direct-hire authorities: qualified NRCS technical-assistance candidates subject to OPM qualification standards, and qualified defined Job Corps graduates for Forest Service competitive-service positions. Both retain the printed exceptions for5USC3303 and3328 within the specified subchapter-I waiver.3303 concerns Congressional recommendations;3328 concerns Selective Service registration with its veteran exception and knowing-and-willful adjudication safeguards. The Job Corps graduate definition concerns actual voluntary selection/enrollment and educational or career-training completion; it is not a synonym for any former enrollee or a newly created immigration classification. No general citizenship, work-authorization, Selective Service or qualification waiver, actual appointment or individual registration determination is inferred.

7608 requires the specified interagency research activities to be applied consistently with CHIPS divisionB/titleVI/subtitleD. The preserved original subtitle and dated19231-19237 comparator distinguish research-agency personnel from covered award individuals, require the stated disclosures/certifications/training, retain proof, privacy and rebuttal/appeal safeguards, preserve qualified open international collaboration and foreign-student advising, and prohibit targeting or discrimination based on race, ethnicity or national origin. They are not a blanket prohibition on foreign students or foreign-born researchers.7614 separately concerns vertebrate-animal research, education or extension in or with China, Russia or defined countries of concern, with its sole-official, necessity and30day-notice waiver; it does not bar all international science or all people from those countries. No actual agency policy, listing, misconduct or nationality determination is made.

9012's solar-component funding exclusion and10006's microorganism pilot use different actors and predicates. The former concerns specified components made in a defined country of concern or by the named domiciled/controlled entity or defined foreign entity of concern. The latter requires an eligible responsible legal entity with a United States physical address, no specified government ownership/affiliation and every other printed experience, facility, containment and compliance predicate. Its75party interstate-microorganism pilot, inspection, release-reporting, disenrollment and appeal provisions govern plant pests, not the admission or removal of people. The CHIPS country and entity definitions retain all their own listed/designated, ownership/control, allegation-plus-conviction and determination branches. No automatic finding that a foreign company, individual or laboratory satisfies them is made.

12301-12305 revise AFIDA information sharing, reporting/enforcement, database and agricultural-transaction review. The original3501 reporting obligations and3508 individual, entity, government, land and State definitions are separately preserved. The individual citizenship/nationality/permanent-residence/parole words and literal disjunctions are not silently changed to a conjunction or converted into a universal present-law classification. The January1,2024 regulation781.2 separately retains its agricultural-land, interest exclusions and significant-interest/control definitions; it does not certify the future enactment-date regulation incorporated by12304.12301 distinguishes nonreporting's maximum25percent penalty from knowingly incomplete/misleading/false reporting's5-25percent range; public identification concerns persons who paid a penalty, with an appeal completed where applicable, not a finding that every foreign owner violated the law. The rulemaking, investigation, outreach and database provisions do not establish actual misconduct or ownership.

12302's covered foreign person requires both the incorporated AFIDA foreign-person definition and citizenship in, or headquarters in, a covered country as applicable. A title about state sponsors does not replace that operative definition.12303's newly incorporated foreign-entity-of-concern definition is15USC4651, distinct from42USC19237; its natural-person protected-individual exclusion and other entity/control/agency branches remain separate. The printed phrases about citizenship/headquarters in a foreign entity of concern and the government of such an entity are retained as printed, with their legal application unresolved.12304 defines 'database' by reference to(c) while development is in(b); no repair is supplied. It withholds the name and price from public disclosure for at least30days; this is not automatic unrestricted publication on day31.

12305 makes Agriculture a CFIUS member for the specified covered agricultural transactions. Its reportable-land transaction has all three printed predicates, including reason to believe based on intelligence information/cooperation, acquisition by the listed four-country foreign person and an AFIDA reporting requirement. CFIUS must determine coverage and, only if covered, whether to initiate review or take another authorized action; not every transaction automatically receives a full review. Its sunset is country-specific removal from the referenced regulatory list.12306 separately directs presidentially ordered regulations prohibiting land purchase by defined foreign adversaries, state sponsors, their agents/instrumentalities and owned/controlled/affiliated persons. Its foreign-adversary definition is conduct-based, not every noncitizen. Neither clause is a new visa, admission or removal ground. The differing printed50USC4318/4813 citations and entity/country words are not normalized; integration, actual lists and individual ownership/legal consequences remain unresolved.

12003 permits additional detector-dog training facilities with the existing Beagle Brigade section2(b) duties, and State/local agriculture cooperative training. Ports of entry, international passenger/cargo volume and regional agricultural pest threats are considerations. The incorporated law concerns dogs and handlers safeguarding agricultural and natural resources from pests and diseases, including CBP collaboration; it does not supply a general power to arrest or remove migrants.12005's separate documentation, vaccination, age, permits, exceptions, denial of entry, quarantine and removal govern imported dogs.12405 concerns information about detained imported plants under the Lacey Act. Likewise the southern-border conservation initiative in2202(f), conditional native-language producer assistance in2502(l), Sequoia project information in English and the affected community's predominant language, colonias, international goods and Mexico water deliveries retain their own geographic or service purposes. None alone establishes a person's citizenship, unlawful presence or entitlement.

This remains one source-qualified candidate for the recorded whole passage. The whole EH, rule, PartA and selected final-floor witness preserve the adopted versus failed amendment and prospective-engrossment boundaries. No component endorsement, motive, current regulation, individual eligibility, factual violation, enactment, implementation, award, admission, removal or achieved outcome is inferred. Independent source/domain review and all reserved legal questions remain; candidate screening is not editorial acceptance or publication authority.

It permits whole milk; it does not require every child to drink it or newly create lunch authority.

TitleIII changes international food assistance as part of the wider package.3101 transfers the defined Food for Peace authorities/assets/liabilities from USAID to USDA at enactment, covering authorities held fromJanuary1,2026 onward, with State consultation.3102 narrows emergency overriding authority from any other LAW to this ACT, adds eligible NGOs and limits non-US-commodity/ocean-transport expenses to50percent of available TitleII funds.3103 repeals1724's tonnage/nonemergency and processed/fortified/bagged-commodity minima with their waivers; it does not repeal every dollar minimum.3110 retains the nonemergency$365million floor/30percent ceiling and adds$200million annually for2027-2031 from emergency TitleII funds for ready-to-use therapeutic child-wasting food ONLY when the latest specified under-five wasting estimate exceeds5percent AND annual TitleII funds exceed$1.2billion. This uses available funds, not a new unconditional appropriation.3106 requires at least$15million annually for2027-2031 from available TitleII funds for the food-relief partnership, available until spent; related consultation, quality and oversight/reporting remain.3308 extends McGovern-Dole and changes developing-country local/regional procurement from up-to10percent to8-15percent. Adding lower-middle-income countries concerns payment of internal transport/storage/handling costs under1736o-1(c)(2)(B), not general eligibility for every food-assistance activity; underlying poverty/net-food-import/education conditions remain. These programs include school food and defined child/pregnant/nursing nutrition assistance, not evidence that assistance was delivered.

The temporal baseline matters. Public Law119-37 section5002 already extends specified2018 farm authorities through the later ofSeptember30,2026 or later applicable statutory dates, subject to its exceptions and appropriation conditions. Printed2023 expiries in amended clauses do not establish that every program had already ended. Public Law119-21's prior SNAP eligibility/work-rule/cost-sharing and SNAP-Ed changes are distinct current law; this passage vote does not newly enact those earlier changes or repeal them wholesale. Floor opponents opposed the package and argued that it fails to undo earlier SNAP cuts and permits problematic contracting; floor proponents defended the provisions and urged passage. These are attributed competing arguments, not adopted fiscal/participation estimates, causal findings, motives or proof of health outcomes. Adopted Luna28 removed the three specified pesticide regulatory/liability sections before passage; the earlier general debate about those sections cannot establish that they remained in the final package. The floor opponent's inserted relief/recommittal text was an unoffered alternative; roll153 is a failed bare recommittal, not support/opposition to that printed substitute.

A Yea supported passage of this entire exact farm package, including its qualified nutrition, rural-care and social-service provisions. A Nay opposed passage of that package. Neither establishes separate positions on SNAP contracting, hot chicken, food guidelines, clinical refinancing, pesticides or any other component, or a preferred alternative. House passage is not enactment, funded awards, restored benefits, achieved food/care access or predicted fiscal/nutrition outcomes.

Immigration qualification of this same whole-passage choice is grounded in the explicit loan eligibility operators, with the other cross-border and personal-status references kept in their own scopes. The complete 959629-character governed EH was read through the attestation and footer. That reading is not an independent raw-HTML or complete Congressional Record reconstruction, a certificate of current-law integration, or editorial acceptance. All original unapproved Health meaning, source identities, claim bindings and limitations above remain part of this same core. Yea supports and Nay opposes passage of the entire package; neither establishes a separate position on any mechanism below.

Sections5101 and5201 replace each printed 'a majority' in the second sentence of7USC1922(a)(1) and1941(a)(1) with 'at least a 50 percent'. In the separately retained2024 statutory parents, that sentence applies conditions including United States citizenship to individual applicants and, for the named entity forms, individuals holding the specified interest. The proposal changes that statutory interest threshold, including the exactly50percent boundary, without deleting the citizenship words or converting every other condition into citizenship. Direct-loan experience, family-farm/operator and inability-to-obtain-credit predicates remain distinct. Section5301 likewise replaces the printed majority threshold in the first sentence of1961(a), whose individual and entity-interest clauses include citizenship, while reorganizing that subsection. This is a source-grounded reason to propose Immigration membership; it is not a conclusion that a particular noncitizen becomes eligible, that only citizens currently qualify, or that the bill supplies immigration status or work authorization.

The loan baselines have a material qualification: the separately preserved January1,2024 direct-loan regulation764.101(c) also names United States noncitizen nationals and qualified aliens for applicants and note signers. The guaranteed-loan regulation762.120(d) separately names those classes, requires the majority entity interest to be held by members in the listed classes, and requires appropriate immigration-status documentation for noncitizen nationals and qualified aliens. These are dated regulatory comparators, not a substituted text of the bill's statutory amendments or an adjudication of their interaction. Later regulations, other controlling law, exact entity structures, signature obligations and individual applications remain for legal/source review. No numerical beneficial-ownership calculation or beneficiary finding is made.

The adjacent loan operators must not be collapsed into that threshold.5101 adds qualified-operator, operating-only entity and embedded-entity rules. Its operating-only rule requires one or more real-estate owners to own at least50percent, or the other percentage the Secretary determines appropriate, of the applicant; its embedded rule retains the at-least75percent condition in its own terms.5201 changes its own operating-loan paragraph and5301 supplies separate emergency-loan rules. In the dated1961(a) parent, the fifth sentence deleted by5301 is the embedded-entity direct-ownership sentence; the bill adds replacement special rules rather than deleting citizenship or all disaster/credit predicates.12420 separately brings defined commercial fishing and fish processing into the named loan definitions and purposes, with different permitted ownership-loan and operating-loan uses and implementation steps. These provisions do not establish that every fishery participant receives a loan or that personal eligibility predicates are waived.

3306 creates a two-way agricultural cultural-immersion and exchange program. The outgoing eligible candidate must meet all four printed conditions: age19-30, demonstrated relevant experience, preparation to live in one or more host countries for the printed two-to-six-month period, and United States residence. Incoming placement in United States host families expressly requires the age condition and residence in an eligible country; it does not simply import all four outgoing conditions. The purpose's reference to developing United States citizens does not rewrite the eligibility word 'resident' into 'citizen'. Eligible countries have agricultural trade relations recognized by the named Service. Administration requires a qualified nonprofit cooperative agreement, the specified memorandum-of-understanding priority and equal non-Federal matching funds.10million dollars annually for2027-2031 is authorization, not proof of appropriation, placement, visa issuance, admission or work permission.7118's separate international institutional partnerships and outgoing internships/fellowships likewise do not themselves establish personal admission status.

2502(g) and8507 provide different discretionary direct-hire authorities: qualified NRCS technical-assistance candidates subject to OPM qualification standards, and qualified defined Job Corps graduates for Forest Service competitive-service positions. Both retain the printed exceptions for5USC3303 and3328 within the specified subchapter-I waiver.3303 concerns Congressional recommendations;3328 concerns Selective Service registration with its veteran exception and knowing-and-willful adjudication safeguards. The Job Corps graduate definition concerns actual voluntary selection/enrollment and educational or career-training completion; it is not a synonym for any former enrollee or a newly created immigration classification. No general citizenship, work-authorization, Selective Service or qualification waiver, actual appointment or individual registration determination is inferred.

7608 requires the specified interagency research activities to be applied consistently with CHIPS divisionB/titleVI/subtitleD. The preserved original subtitle and dated19231-19237 comparator distinguish research-agency personnel from covered award individuals, require the stated disclosures/certifications/training, retain proof, privacy and rebuttal/appeal safeguards, preserve qualified open international collaboration and foreign-student advising, and prohibit targeting or discrimination based on race, ethnicity or national origin. They are not a blanket prohibition on foreign students or foreign-born researchers.7614 separately concerns vertebrate-animal research, education or extension in or with China, Russia or defined countries of concern, with its sole-official, necessity and30day-notice waiver; it does not bar all international science or all people from those countries. No actual agency policy, listing, misconduct or nationality determination is made.

9012's solar-component funding exclusion and10006's microorganism pilot use different actors and predicates. The former concerns specified components made in a defined country of concern or by the named domiciled/controlled entity or defined foreign entity of concern. The latter requires an eligible responsible legal entity with a United States physical address, no specified government ownership/affiliation and every other printed experience, facility, containment and compliance predicate. Its75party interstate-microorganism pilot, inspection, release-reporting, disenrollment and appeal provisions govern plant pests, not the admission or removal of people. The CHIPS country and entity definitions retain all their own listed/designated, ownership/control, allegation-plus-conviction and determination branches. No automatic finding that a foreign company, individual or laboratory satisfies them is made.

12301-12305 revise AFIDA information sharing, reporting/enforcement, database and agricultural-transaction review. The original3501 reporting obligations and3508 individual, entity, government, land and State definitions are separately preserved. The individual citizenship/nationality/permanent-residence/parole words and literal disjunctions are not silently changed to a conjunction or converted into a universal present-law classification. The January1,2024 regulation781.2 separately retains its agricultural-land, interest exclusions and significant-interest/control definitions; it does not certify the future enactment-date regulation incorporated by12304.12301 distinguishes nonreporting's maximum25percent penalty from knowingly incomplete/misleading/false reporting's5-25percent range; public identification concerns persons who paid a penalty, with an appeal completed where applicable, not a finding that every foreign owner violated the law. The rulemaking, investigation, outreach and database provisions do not establish actual misconduct or ownership.

12302's covered foreign person requires both the incorporated AFIDA foreign-person definition and citizenship in, or headquarters in, a covered country as applicable. A title about state sponsors does not replace that operative definition.12303's newly incorporated foreign-entity-of-concern definition is15USC4651, distinct from42USC19237; its natural-person protected-individual exclusion and other entity/control/agency branches remain separate. The printed phrases about citizenship/headquarters in a foreign entity of concern and the government of such an entity are retained as printed, with their legal application unresolved.12304 defines 'database' by reference to(c) while development is in(b); no repair is supplied. It withholds the name and price from public disclosure for at least30days; this is not automatic unrestricted publication on day31.

12305 makes Agriculture a CFIUS member for the specified covered agricultural transactions. Its reportable-land transaction has all three printed predicates, including reason to believe based on intelligence information/cooperation, acquisition by the listed four-country foreign person and an AFIDA reporting requirement. CFIUS must determine coverage and, only if covered, whether to initiate review or take another authorized action; not every transaction automatically receives a full review. Its sunset is country-specific removal from the referenced regulatory list.12306 separately directs presidentially ordered regulations prohibiting land purchase by defined foreign adversaries, state sponsors, their agents/instrumentalities and owned/controlled/affiliated persons. Its foreign-adversary definition is conduct-based, not every noncitizen. Neither clause is a new visa, admission or removal ground. The differing printed50USC4318/4813 citations and entity/country words are not normalized; integration, actual lists and individual ownership/legal consequences remain unresolved.

12003 permits additional detector-dog training facilities with the existing Beagle Brigade section2(b) duties, and State/local agriculture cooperative training. Ports of entry, international passenger/cargo volume and regional agricultural pest threats are considerations. The incorporated law concerns dogs and handlers safeguarding agricultural and natural resources from pests and diseases, including CBP collaboration; it does not supply a general power to arrest or remove migrants.12005's separate documentation, vaccination, age, permits, exceptions, denial of entry, quarantine and removal govern imported dogs.12405 concerns information about detained imported plants under the Lacey Act. Likewise the southern-border conservation initiative in2202(f), conditional native-language producer assistance in2502(l), Sequoia project information in English and the affected community's predominant language, colonias, international goods and Mexico water deliveries retain their own geographic or service purposes. None alone establishes a person's citizenship, unlawful presence or entitlement.

actions.candidate_short_description: Whole Farm Bill passage with qualified citizenship-linked loan eligibility and distinct cross-border mechanisms
actions.candidate_compact_description: Pass the whole exact Farm Bill, including literal entity-interest changes in citizenship-linked loan predicates, conditional exchange and agricultural inspection provisions. Dated regulatory/definition differences and individual legal applications remain qualified; no component stance or enacted outcome.
candidate_shared_limitations: One whole farm package; component choices and voice/unrecorded amendment outcomes do not establish separate member positions or a preferred alternative.
Adopted4114/4115 remain separate amendment choices145/146; failed151 soda restriction is not a package component. Luna28 removed10205-10207; earlier debate does not establish their retention.
Conditional1224 section11 prospective1346 engrossment is not a recorded1346 passage or a license to borrow future text; technical corrections do not create a new policy choice.
ExistingPL119-37 farm extensions andPL119-21 SNAP changes qualify printed dates/current law. This vote neither newly enacts earlier SNAP cuts nor restores the eliminated SNAP-Ed grant program.

Amounts labeled authorization require appropriations; single available-until-spent milk/HFFI totals are not annual amounts. Mandatory senior-market funding and contingent child-wasting set-asides retain their distinct force.

SNAP contracting retains triggers, merit/blended-staff, no-denial-incentive, retailer-interest, notification, expiry and collective-bargaining limits. Incentive categories do not limit ordinary SNAP benefit purchases.

School95percent rule is by designated food category with unavailable-item and existing geographic scope, not an unqualified nationwide percentage of all spending. Breakfast milk extends existing lunch law with nondairy/nutritional protections.

Rural care retains program-specific eligibility, feasibility/security, planning, discretionary waiver, technical-assistance caps and rulemaking effective date; not uniform50,000-person eligibility or universal treatment.

Food-aid tonnage repeal does not repeal all dollar minima; therapeutic-food funds require BOTH wasting and available-fund thresholds. Lower-middle-income addition concerns specified internal cost payments.
Victim/animal housing retains confidentiality and no forced participation/services,24months plus conditional extension, defined entities/populations and administration cap.
Research, reports and guidelines do not establish treatment, restrictions, compliance or outcomes. Attributed contrary floor arguments remain claims; House passage alone is not enactment or delivery.
Source-qualified Immigration augmentation changes no original Health prefix, source identity, claim binding or limit; all source/domain/editorial acceptance remains pending.

Statutory majority-to-atleast50percent wording and dated regulatory citizenship/noncitizen-national/qualified-alien predicates are distinct; no actual entity/person eligibility, automatic benefit, visa, work authorization, admission or removal determination.

AFIDA literal disjunctions, entity/country wording, foreign-entity definitions, printed citations and database cross-reference remain unrepaired; current integration, ownership/listings and individual legal applications unresolved.

Dog and plant import inspection/removal, agricultural pests, geographic/service references and international commodities do not by themselves establish personal Immigration meaning; whole package and separate amendment choices remain distinct.

Complete captured EH and selected floor/rule/PartA reading do not certify raw HTML, entire Record/report/Print, every current regulation or enacted outcome. All denied/cancelled source and publication boundaries remain.

claim_source_map.passage: SEC. 4103. SNAP STAFFING FLEXIBILITY. Section 11 of the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008 (7 U.S.C. 2020) is amended by adding at the end the following: ``(y) SNAP Staffing Flexibility.-- ``(1) In general.--Notwithstanding section 11(e)(6)(B), a State agency (as defined in section 3 of the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008) may, by contract with the State agency at a reasonable cost in accordance with the State agency's standard contracting rules, hire a contractor to undertake supplemental nutrition assistance program certification or carry out any other function of the State agency under such program so long as-- ``(A) the contract does not provide incentives for the agency or contractor to delay eligibility determinations or to deny eligibility for individuals otherwise eligible for supplemental nutrition assistance program benefits; and ``(B) the contractor has no direct or indirect financial interest in an approved retail store. ``(2) Use.--A State agency may use the authority provided in paragraph (1) when-- ``(A) the State experiences an inability to timely process supplemental nutrition assistance program applications from causes that include but are not limited to-- ``(i) pandemics and other health emergencies; ``(ii) seasonal workforce cycles; ``(iii) temporary staffing shortages; and ``(iv) weather or other natural disasters; ``(B) the State's payment error rate, as defined in section 16, is greater than or equal to 6 percent based on the most recent available Department of Agriculture data; or ``(C) the State experiences an increase in supplemental nutrition assistance program applications. ``(3) Requirements.--A State agency that hires a contractor under paragraph (1) shall ensure such action-- ``(A) is consistent with all principles under section 900.603 of title 5 of the Code of Federal Regulations; and ``(B) is part of a blended workforce and does not supplant existing merit-based personnel in the State. ``(4) Notification.--A State agency shall notify the Secretary of its intent to use the authority provided in this section and shall provide any information or data supporting State agency increases in supplemental nutrition assistance program applications or any inability to timely process such applications. ``(5) Public availability.--Not later than 10 days after the date of the receipt of a notification submitted by a State agency under paragraph (4), the Secretary shall make publicly available on the website of the Department of Agriculture the notification submitted by such State agency and any accompanying information or data supporting such notification so submitted. ``(6) Program design.--Any action taken by a State agency under paragraph (1) shall not be-- ``(A) considered to be a major change in the operations of such State agency for purposes of section 11(a)(4) of this Act, or ``(B) subject to any requirement specified in such section. ``(7) Annual report.--The Secretary shall submit to the Committee on Agriculture of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry of the Senate, an annual report that contains-- ``(A) a description of measures taken to address increases in supplemental nutrition assistance program applications and any inability to timely process such applications; ``(B) information or data supporting State agency notifications provided pursuant to paragraph (4); and ``(C) recommendations for changes to the Secretary's authority under this Act to assist the Secretary, States, and local governments of States in preparing for any future increases in supplemental nutrition assistance program applications or inability to timely process such applications. ``(8) Temporary staffing shortages.--In cases of temporary staffing shortages, the authority provided to State agencies under paragraph (1) shall-- ``(A) expire when the backlog of supplemental nutrition assistance program applications has been eliminated; ``(B) not override any collective bargaining agreement or memorandum of understanding in effect between the State and employees of the State or of a local government of such State; and ``(C) expire when the error rate, as defined in section 16, is less than 6 percent.''.

claim_source_map.passage: SEC. 4204. COMMODITY SUPPLEMENTAL FOOD PROGRAM DEMONSTRATION PROJECT FOR TRIBAL ORGANIZATIONS. (a) Demonstration Project for Tribal Organizations.-- (1) Definitions.--In this subsection: (A) Demonstration project.--The term ``demonstration project'' means the demonstration project established under paragraph (2). (B) Food distribution program.--The term ``food distribution program'' means the commodity supplemental food program identified in section 4 of the Agriculture and Consumer Protection Act of 1973 (7 U.S.C. 612c note; Public Law 93-86). (C) Indian reservation.--The term ``Indian reservation'' has the meaning given the term ``reservation'' in section 3 of the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008 (7 U.S.C. 2012). (D) Indian tribe.--The term ``Indian Tribe'' has the meaning given the term in section 4 of the Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act (25 U.S.C. 5304). (E) Self-determination contract.--The term ``self- determination contract'' has the meaning given the term in section 4 of the Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act (25 U.S.C. 5304) with modification as determined by the Secretary. (F) Tribal organization.--The term ``Tribal organization'' has the meaning given the term in section 3 of the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008 (7 U.S.C. 2012). (2) Establishment.--Subject to the availability of appropriations, the Secretary shall establish a demonstration project under which 1 or more Tribal organizations may enter into self-determination contracts to purchase agricultural commodities under the food distribution program for the Indian reservation of that Tribal organization. (3) Eligibility.-- (A) Consultation.--The Secretary shall consult with Indian Tribes to determine the process and criteria under which a Tribal organization may participate in the demonstration project. (B) Criteria.--The Secretary shall select for participation in the demonstration project Tribal organizations that-- (i) are successfully administering the food distribution program of the Tribal organization under section 4(b)(2)(B) of the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008 (7 U.S.C. 2013(b)(2)(B)); (ii) have the capacity to purchase agricultural commodities in accordance with paragraph (4) for the food distribution program of the Tribal organization; and (iii) meet any other criteria determined by the Secretary, in consultation with the Secretary of the Interior and Indian Tribes. (4) Procurement of agricultural commodities.--Any agricultural commodities purchased by a Tribal organization under the demonstration project shall-- (A) be domestically produced; (B) not result in a material increase in the amount of food in the food package of that Tribal organization compared to the amount of food that the Secretary authorized to be provided through the Commodity Supplemental Food Program Guide Rate; (C) be of similar or higher nutritional value as the type of agricultural commodities that would be supplanted in the existing food package for that Tribal organization or be an agricultural commodity with Tribal significance to that Indian Tribe; and (D) meet any other criteria determined by the Secretary. (5) Report.--Not later than 1 year after the date on which funds are appropriated under paragraph (6) and annually thereafter, the Secretary shall submit to the Committee on Agriculture of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry of the Senate a report describing the activities carried out under the demonstration project during the preceding year. (6) Funding.-- (A) Authorization of appropriations.--There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this subsection $1,000,000, to remain available until expended. (B) Appropriations in advance.--Only funds appropriated under subparagraph (A) in advance specifically to carry out this subsection shall be available to carry out this subsection. (b) Administration of Tribal Self-Determination Contracts.-- (1) Administration.--The Secretary shall appoint an existing office of the United States Department of Agriculture to administer Tribal self-determination contracts to include but not limited to: (A) awarding of Food and Nutrition Service nutrition program self-determination contracts to selected Tribal organizations; and (B) hiring contract officers and program staff in order to manage the selection of Tribal organizations and execution of self-determination contracts. (2) Staffing minimum funding.--Notwithstanding any other provision of law, there is authorized to be appropriated $1,200,000 for each of fiscal years 2027 through 2031 for the payment of Department contract officers and program staff salaries and benefits. Subtitle C--Miscellaneous

claim_source_map.passage: SEC. 4309. FRESH FRUITS AND VEGETABLES CATEGORIZATION. (a) In General.--The Secretary of Agriculture, in coordination with the Secretary of Health and Human Services, shall develop a low-risk classification for fresh fruits, vegetables, and other foods that are typically consumed raw or with minimal processing, and update relevant nutrition and food safety and preparation regulations and guidelines for child care providers in accordance with the classification under this section. (b) Classification.--In developing the classification under this section, the Secretaries shall consider-- (1) the limited risks of food-born illness and negative health impacts associated with handling and preparing fresh fruits, vegetables, and other foods that are typically consumed raw or with minimal processing; (2) best practices to minimize food safety risks without obstructing access to low-risk foods as defined under the classification under this section, including but not limited to access to a handwashing sink; and (3) existing barriers that privilege packaged, processed foods over fresh fruits, vegetables, and other foods that are typically consumed raw or with minimal processing. (c) Implementation.--The Secretaries shall ensure the effective coordination of policies and activities within the Department of Agriculture and the Department of Health and Human Services related to nutrition and food safety and preparation in child care facilities to ensure State regulations that impact such activities reflect the classification under this section and protect child care providers from any penalties as a result of providing children foods in compliance with this section. (d) Compliance.--States that fail to comply with the policies and activities described in subsection (c) may have funds withheld.

claim_source_map.passage: SEC. 4310. PROMOTING ACCESS TO LOCAL AGRICULTURE. (a) Streamlining Applications for Farmers.-- (1) Definitions.--In this section: (A) Covered nutrition program.--The term ``covered nutrition program'' means-- (i) the supplemental nutrition assistance program established under the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008 (7 U.S.C. 2011 et seq.); (ii) the senior farmers' market nutrition program established under section 4402 of the Farm Security and Rural Investment Act of 2002 (7 U.S.C. 3007); (iii) the special supplemental nutrition program for women, infants, and children established by section 17 of the Child Nutrition Act of 1966 (42 U.S.C. 1786), including the farmers' market nutrition program under that program; and (iv) the Gus Schumacher Nutrition Incentive Program established under section 4405 of the Food, Conservation, and Energy Act of 2008 (7 U.S.C. 7517), as practicable with respect to the activities carried out by the Secretary under paragraphs (2) and (3). (B) Secretary.--The term ``Secretary'' means the Secretary of Agriculture. (2) Streamlined application process.-- (A) In general.--The Secretary shall establish a streamlined application process-- (i) for direct marketing farmers and ranchers to apply to be vendors under each of the covered nutrition programs; and (ii) by-- (I) developing a single application that a direct marketing farmer or rancher may use to apply to each of the covered nutrition programs; or (II) developing an information sharing system that-- (aa) shares the information of a direct marketing farmer or rancher who is approved as an authorized vendor under a covered nutrition program with each of the other covered nutrition programs; and (bb) deems that direct marketing farmer or rancher as a prequalified eligible vendor for those other covered nutrition programs. (a) Definitions.--In this section: (1) Childcare.-- (A) In general.--The term ``childcare'' means any program that-- (i) provides quality care and early education for children who have not yet entered first grade; and (ii) is operated by-- (I) an eligible childcare provider described in section 658P(6)(A) of the Child Care and Development Block Grant Act of 1990 (42 U.S.C. 9858n(6)(A)); or (II) a childcare provider that, on the date of enactment of this Act-- (aa) is licensed, regulated, or registered in the State, territory, or Indian Tribe in which the provider is located; and (bb) meets applicable State, Tribal, territorial, and local health and safety requirements. (B) Inclusions.--The term ``childcare'' includes-- (i) a school-based program described in subparagraph (A); (ii) a program described in subparagraph (A) that is a Head Start program, including a migrant and seasonal Head Start program, or an American Indian and Alaska Native Head Start program carried out under the Head Start Act (42 U.S.C. 9831 et seq.); (iii) a facility used for a program described in subparagraph (A); and (iv) a service provided under a program described in subparagraph (A). (2) Initiative.--The term ``Initiative'' means the Expanding Childcare in Rural America Initiative established under subsection (b). (3) Rural area.--The term ``rural area'' has the meaning given the term in section 343(a)(13)(A) of the Consolidated Farm and Rural Development Act. (b) Establishment.--The Secretary shall establish an initiative, to be known as the ``Expanding Childcare in Rural America Initiative'', under which the Secretary shall provide, for each of fiscal years 2027 through 2029, priority in accordance with subsection (c) to address the availability, quality, and cost of childcare in rural areas. (c) Childcare Priorities.-- (1) In general.--Notwithstanding any other provision of law, in selecting recipients of loans and grants under a program described in paragraph (2), the Secretary shall give priority to any qualified applicant that proposes to use the loan or grant to address the availability, quality, or cost of childcare. (2) Description of programs.--The programs referred to in paragraph (1) are the following: (A) The essential community facilities loan and grant programs authorized under section 306(a) of the Consolidated Farm and Rural Development Act (7 U.S.C. 1926(a)). (B) The business and industry direct and guaranteed loan program authorized under section 310B(g) of that Act (7 U.S.C. 1932(g)). (C) The rural microentrepreneur assistance program authorized under section 379E of that Act (7 U.S.C. 2008s). (D) The intermediary relending program authorized under the Food Security Act of 1985 (7 U.S.C. 1936b). (d) Requirements.--In providing funding in accordance with the Initiative, the Secretary shall ensure a balanced geographical distribution of the benefits under the Initiative. (e) Evaluation; Report.-- (1) Evaluation.--Not later than 3 years after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall conduct a comprehensive quantitative and qualitative evaluation of the projects carried out using assistance provided under the Initiative, including-- (A) a description of-- (i) the types of projects carried out; (ii) the communities in which the projects are carried out; (iii) the organizations and entities participating in the projects; and (iv) the types of partnerships developed to carry out the projects; and (B) the economic and social impacts of the investments in the projects. (2) Report.--Not later than 4 years after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall submit to the Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry of the Senate and the Committee on Agriculture of the House of Representatives a report describing the evaluation conducted under paragraph (1), including a thorough analysis of the outcomes of the evaluation.

claim_source_map.passage: (j) Incentives (1) Definition of eligible incentive food In this subsection, the term "eligible incentive food" means— (A) a staple food that is identified for increased consumption, consistent with the most recent dietary recommendations; and (B) a fruit, vegetable, dairy, whole grain, or product thereof. (2) Guidance (A) In general The Secretary shall issue guidance to clarify the process by which an approved retail food store may seek a waiver to offer an incentive, which may be used only for the purchase of an eligible incentive food at the point of purchase, to a household purchasing food with benefits issued under this chapter. (B) Guidance The guidance under subparagraph (A) shall establish a process under which an approved retail food store, prior to carrying out an incentive program under this subsection, shall provide to the Secretary information describing the incentive program, including— (i) the types of incentives that will be offered; (ii) the types of foods that will be incentivized for purchase; and (iii) an explanation of how the incentive program intends to support meeting dietary intake goals. (3) No limitation on benefits A waiver granted under this subsection shall not be used to carry out any activity that limits the use of benefits under this chapter or any other Federal nutrition law. (4) Effect Guidance provided under this subsection shall not affect any requirements under section 7517 of this title, including the eligibility of a retail food store to participate in a project funded under such section. (5) Report The Secretary shall submit to the Committee on Agriculture of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry of the Senate an annual report describing the types of incentives approved under this subsection. claim_source_map.passage: (a) In general (1) The Secretary is also authorized to make or insure loans to associations, including corporations not operated for profit, Indian tribes on Federal and State reservations and other federally recognized Indian tribes, and public and quasi-public agencies to provide for the application or establishment of soil conservation practices, shifts in land use, the conservation, development, use, and control of water, and the installation or improvement of drainage or waste disposal facilities, recreational developments, and essential community facilities including necessary related equipment, all primarily serving farmers, ranchers, farm tenants, farm laborers, rural businesses, and other rural residents, and to furnish financial assistance or other aid in planning projects for such purposes. The Secretary may also make or insure loans to communities that have been designated as rural empowerment zones or rural enterprise communities pursuant to part I of subchapter U of chapter 1 of title 26, or as rural enterprise communities pursuant to section 766 of the Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 1999 (Public Law 105–277; 112 Stat. 2681, 2681–37), to provide for the installation or improvement of essential community facilities including necessary related equipment, and to furnish financial assistance or other aid in planning projects for such purposes. The Secretary may also make loans to any borrower to whom a loan has been made under the Rural Elec trification Act of 1936 (7 U.S.C. 901 et seq.), for the conservation, development, use, and control of water, and the installation of drainage or waste disposal facilities, primarily serving farmers, ranchers, farm tenants, farm laborers, rural businesses, and other rural residents. When any loan made for a purpose specified in this paragraph is sold out of the Agricultural Credit Insurance Fund as an insured loan, the interest or other income thereon paid to an insured holder shall be included in gross income for purposes of chapter 1 of title 26. With respect to loans of less than $500,000 made or insured under this paragraph that are evidenced by notes and mortgages, as distinguished from bond issues, borrowers shall not be required to appoint bond counsel to review the legal validity of the loan whenever the Secretary has available legal counsel to perform such review.

§ 1990a. Refinancing of certain rural hospital 
debt 
Assistance under section 1926(a) of this title 
for a community facility, or under section 1932 
of this title, may include the refinancing of a 
debt obligation of a rural hospital as an eligible 
loan or loan guarantee purpose if the assistance 
would help preserve access to a health service in 
a rural community, meaningfully improve the 
financial position of the hospital, and otherwise 
meet the financial feasibility and adequacy of 
security requirements of the Rural Development 
Agency.
